_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Lesotho covering San rock art, Moshoeshoe I (nation builder), Basotho nation formation, Gun War, Basutoland protectorate, independence 1966, mountain kingdom (entirely above 1000m), Lesotho Highlands Water Project (LHWP), and political instability.

ethnic_groups.name: Basotho (Sotho)
ethnic_groups.notes: Bantu-speaking; forged into nation by Moshoeshoe I 1820s-1860s; Sesotho language; originally refugees from Mfecane/Lifaqane; clans include Koena (royal), Fokeng, Kwena, Tlokwa

current_leader.name: King Letsie III
current_leader.title: King
current_leader.notes: Constitutional monarch; son of Moshoeshoe II; ceremonial role; first abdicated to restore father 1995; returned after father's death 1996

prime_minister.name: Sam Matekane
prime_minister.notes: Revolution for Prosperity (RFP) party; businessman; ended political instability cycle

former_leaders.name: Chief Leabua Jonathan
former_leaders.notes: First PM post-independence; BNP; suspended constitution 1970 after election loss; ousted in 1986 coup

former_leaders.name: Ntsu Mokhehle
former_leaders.notes: BCP founder; won 1993 election; switched to LCD 1997

former_leaders.name: Pakalitha Mosisili
former_leaders.notes: LCD/DC; longest-serving PM; SADC military intervention 1998

former_leaders.name: Thomas Thabane
former_leaders.notes: ABC founder; first coalition government; resigned amid murder case of estranged wife

910.name: San Rock Art and Early Inhabitants
910.description: San hunter-gatherers inhabit the Maloti-Drakensberg mountains for tens of thousands of years, leaving one of the richest rock-art traditions in southern Africa.

sub_clusters.name: Stone Age Highland Settlements
sub_clusters.description: Middle and Later Stone Age tools found in rock shelters across the Lesotho highlands; evidence of seasonal transhumance patterns.

sub_clusters.name: San Rock Art of the Maloti-Drakensberg
sub_clusters.description: Thousands of polychrome rock paintings depicting eland hunts, rain-making rituals, and therianthropic (half-human/half-animal) trance figures; among the finest in the world.

920.name: Bantu Migration and Early Sotho Communities
920.description: Bantu-speaking peoples settle the region; Sotho-Tswana communities develop distinct cultural and political identities in the highlands.

sub_clusters.name: Early Bantu Settlement
sub_clusters.description: Bantu-speaking farmers arrive from the north, introducing iron-working, sorghum cultivation, and cattle keeping; interaction with and gradual displacement of San populations.

sub_clusters.name: Formation of Sotho Chiefdoms
sub_clusters.description: Sotho-speaking groups (Bakwena, Bafokeng, Bataung, Basia) establish chiefdoms in the highland valleys; cattle-based economy; stone-walled settlement sites.

930.name: Moshoeshoe I and the Basotho Nation
930.description: Moshoeshoe I (c.1786–1870), one of Africa's greatest statesmen, unites diverse refugees of the Difaqane into the Basotho nation from his mountain fortress of Thaba Bosiu.

sub_clusters.name: Moshoeshoe's Rise and Thaba Bosiu
sub_clusters.description: Born Lepoqo of the Bamokoteli; renamed Moshoeshoe ('the Shaver'); moves followers to impregnable flat-topped mountain of Thaba Bosiu in 1824.

sub_clusters.name: Basotho Nation Formation during Difaqane
sub_clusters.description: Moshoeshoe shelters and absorbs refugees from Zulu, Ndebele, and Griqua raids; builds a new multi-clan nation through diplomacy, cattle-loaning (mafisa), and strategic marriages.

sub_clusters.name: Wars with Orange Free State Boers
sub_clusters.description: Three wars with the Orange Free State over fertile lowlands; Moshoeshoe loses the Conquered Territory but successfully appeals to Queen Victoria for British protection.

940.name: Basutoland Protectorate
940.description: British Basutoland protectorate preserved from South African incorporation; the Gun War demonstrates Basotho resistance; migrant labour to South African mines reshapes society.

sub_clusters.name: The Gun War (1880–1881)
sub_clusters.description: Basotho refuse Cape Colony's attempt to disarm them; successful resistance leads to direct British imperial control rather than Cape administration; only southern African people never fully conquered.

sub_clusters.name: British Colonial Administration
sub_clusters.description: Indirect rule through paramount chief and district chiefs; Basutoland National Council established 1903; deliberate underdevelopment; territory remains surrounded by South Africa.

sub_clusters.name: Migrant Labour System
sub_clusters.description: Basotho men become major workforce in South African gold and diamond mines; remittances become economic backbone; social disruption of absent husbands and fathers.

950.name: Independence and Early Political Struggles
950.description: Lesotho gains independence in 1966; Chief Leabua Jonathan's authoritarian rule; conflict between BNP and BCP; South African economic and military pressure.

sub_clusters.name: Lesotho Independence 1966
sub_clusters.description: Constitutional development; Basutoland Congress Party (BCP) vs Basotho National Party (BNP); independence on 4 October 1966 under King Moshoeshoe II and PM Leabua Jonathan.

sub_clusters.name: Leabua Jonathan's Authoritarian Rule
sub_clusters.description: Jonathan suspends constitution after losing 1970 election; declares state of emergency; Lesotho Liberation Army insurgency; South African blockade 1986 leads to military coup.

950.name: Military Rule and Democratic Transition
950.description: Military junta 1986–1993; democratic transition; King Moshoeshoe II's exile and return; political instability continues.

sub_clusters.name: Military Junta 1986–1993
sub_clusters.description: General Lekhanya overthrows Jonathan; restores executive powers to King Moshoeshoe II then exiles him; Major General Ramaema takes over 1991; transition to elections.

sub_clusters.name: 1993 Democratic Elections
sub_clusters.description: BCP wins all 65 seats; factional politics; King Moshoeshoe II returns and dies in car accident 1996; King Letsie III ascends; 1998 election dispute triggers SADC intervention.

960.name: Modern Lesotho: Mountain Kingdom Challenges
960.description: Lesotho navigates post-intervention reforms, the Highlands Water Project, HIV/AIDS crisis, political instability, and economic dependence on South Africa.

sub_clusters.name: Lesotho Highlands Water Project
sub_clusters.description: Massive engineering project supplying water to South Africa's Gauteng province; Phase I completed 2003; Phase II (Polihali Dam) under construction; royalties fund Lesotho's budget.

sub_clusters.name: Political Instability and Attempted Coups
sub_clusters.description: PM Tom Thabane's coalition politics; Lieutenant General Kamoli's 2014 attempted coup; SADC mediates; Thabane charged with murder of ex-wife; multiple snap elections.

sub_clusters.name: HIV/AIDS and Textile Economy
sub_clusters.description: Second-highest HIV prevalence globally; AGOA-driven textile industry becomes largest private employer; decline of mine remittances; food insecurity in highlands.

sub_clusters.name: Constitutional Reform Process
sub_clusters.description: SADC-mandated constitutional reforms (Phumaphi Commission) to address political instability; debates over powers of prime minister, monarchy, and military; implementation delays.
